Name: Patch Information Version A
Description: The Patch Information Version A (PATCHA) TRE provides information describing a portion of an image, a patch, to support exploitation. In order to achieve the specified resolution in a SAR image, the phase history data must be continuously collected over a calculated flight path distance; this batch of phase history is then processed into one SAR image patch. This TRE contains support data pertaining to a single image patch, and one extension is created for each image patch.

PAT_NO.Name: Patch Number
PAT_NO.Description: This field contains the patch number. Patches are numbered consecutively, starting with 0001 for each image within a file.

LAST_PAT_FLAG.Name: Last Patch of Search Scene
LAST_PAT_FLAG.Description: This field contains a flag to indicate that this is the last patch in a search scene. When all patches of a scene are not contained within a single patch image, PATCH_TOT in ACFTB cannot indicate the total number of patches in the scene; this flag then makes it clear that the scene ends with this patch. 0 = Not End, 1 = End.

LNSTRT.Name: Line Start
LNSTRT.Description: This field contains the absolute starting line number of this patch within an overall image (scene). This field provides similar information to ILOC in the image subheader, but in a form more suitable for some operations. LNSTRT identifies specifically where this patch fits relative to the other N patches comprising an overall scene, whereas relative values in ILOC are referenced to the object to which this patch is attached.

LNSTOP.Name: Line Stop
LNSTOP.Description: This field contains the absolute ending line number of this patch within an overall image (scene). This field provides similar information to ILOC in the image subheader, but in a form more suitable for some operations. LNSTRT identifies specifically where this patch fits relative to the other N patches comprising an overall scene, whereas relative values in ILOC are referenced to the object to which this patch is attached.

AZL.Name: Azimuth Lines
AZL.Description: This field contains the number of azimuth lines in the current patch.

NVL.Name: Number of Valid Azimuth Lines
NVL.Description: This field contains the number of valid azimuth lines. The Spot mode frame dimensions are 2,720 azimuth lines by 2,720 range pixels. In the Continuous Spot mode, the Spot scene does not always completely fill the frame. Therefore, NVL together with FVL describe the location of the valid imagery within the 2,720 azimuth lines transferred. This variable has no meaning in Search mode.

FVL.Name: First Valid Line
FVL.Description: This field contains the first valid azimuth line. The Spot mode frame dimensions are 2,720 azimuth lines by 2,720 range pixels. In the Continuous Spot mode, the Spot scene does not always completely fill the frame. Therefore, FVL together with NVL describe the location of the valid imagery within the 2,720 azimuth lines transferred. This variable has no meaning in Search mode.

NPIXEL.Name: Number of Image Pixels
NPIXEL.Description: This field contains the number of image pixels per line. The value range for Spot is 00170 to 06000 and the value range for Search is 00272 to 08160.

FVPIX.Name: First Valid Pixel Index
FVPIX.Description: This field contains the location of the first pixel on a line. This variable, with the number of pixels per line, will define the location of the image within the 8,160 pixels per line for Search and 2,720 for Spot. The value range for Spot is 00001 to 02551 and the value range for Search is 00001 to 07889.

FRAME.Name: Spot Frame Number
FRAME.Description: This field contains the spot frame number. In Continuous Spot Mode, each image about the same Map Center (a single scene) is called a Frame. The Frame Number starts at 1 and is incremented by 1 for each frame of the scene. The value of this field contains spaces for Search and Single Spot modes.

UTC.Name: Coordinated Universal Time
UTC.Description: This field contains the time in seconds (accurate to 0.01 seconds) of the start of the current patch or, in the cases of Spot, the current scene or frame. UTC uses a 24-hour clock where a value of 00000.00 corresponds to midnight.

SHEAD.Name: Scene Heading
SHEAD.Description: The Scene Heading is a variable that references the scene to True North. In Search scenes, it is the angle from True North to the Scene CenterLine. In Spotlight Scenes, it is the angle from True North to the Azimuth Vector.

GRAVITY.Name: Local Gravity
GRAVITY.Description: This field contains the local gravity, defined in feet/seconds^2.

INS_V_NC.Name: Ins Platform Velocity, North
INS_V_NC.Description: The Inertial Navigator Platform velocity is given in a North, East, Down earth-fixed coordinate system. This parameter is valid at the time specified by UTC.

INS_V_EC.Name: Ins Platform Velocity, East
INS_V_EC.Description: The Inertial Navigator Platform velocity is given in a North, East, Down earth-fixed coordinate system. This parameter is valid at the time specified by UTC.

INS_V_DC.Name: Ins Platform Velocity, Down
INS_V_DC.Description: The Inertial Navigator Platform velocity is given in a North, East, Down earth-fixed coordinate system. This parameter is valid at the time specified by UTC.

OFFLAT.Name: Geodetic Latitude Offset
OFFLAT.Description: The Geodetic Latitude Offset is the accumulated latitude correction currently being used to correct the Inertial Navigation System (INS) aircraft position outputs. The offset is given in seconds of a degree; North and East are positive.

OFFLONG.Name: Geodetic Longitude Offset
OFFLONG.Description: The Geodetic Longitude Offset is the accumulated longitude correction currently being used to correct the Inertial Navigation System (INS) aircraft position outputs. The offset is given in seconds of a degree; North and East are positive.

TRACK.Name: Track Heading
TRACK.Description: The track heading is measured in degrees relative to True North. The measurement is clockwise about the vertical from North to the projection of the aircraft roll axis into the level plane, and is valid at the time specified by UTC.

GSWEEP.Name: Ground Sweep Angle
GSWEEP.Description: The ground sweep angle is determined by the required azimuth resolution and is the angle over which phase history is collected. The measurements are given in degrees.

SHEAR.Name: Patch Shear Factor
SHEAR.Description: This field describes the patch shear factor. Targets are imagined in the slant plane determined by the Processing Central Reference Point and the SAR velocity vector at mid-array. The conversion from target spacing in the ground plane to target spacing in the slant plane for each patch allows the optimal matching of terrain features in one patch to those in the next.
